body:
Look through almost any vape catalog and you will see the same flavor offered twice, once plain and once with "ice", "freeze", "frost" or "chill" in the name. Strawberry and strawberry ice, watermelon and watermelon ice, blue razz and blue razz ice. The ice versions are some of the most popular products on the market, and they work by adding a cooling sensation to the flavor. This guide explains what cooling agents are, how they create the sensation of cold without any change in temperature, how ice flavors differ from mint and menthol, how cooling changes the taste of fruit, how intense versions vary, how to choose, who might prefer plain flavors and what to do if cooling is too strong. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive. We make no health claims about flavorings or cooling agents, and nothing here is medical advice.

## What cooling agents are
Cooling agents are flavor ingredients that trigger the cold-sensing nerves in your mouth and throat. Menthol, from mint plants or made synthetically, is the best-known. Other compounds do the same job with less minty taste, and makers use them to add a cool, clean finish to fruit and other flavors. The vapor is not actually colder. The sensation is created by the way the compounds interact with receptors that normally detect cold. That is why a warm vapor can feel icy.

## Ice versus mint and menthol
A mint or menthol flavor is built around the minty taste, with cooling as part of the character. An ice flavor is usually a fruit or other flavor with cooling added on top, so the fruit stays recognizable and the cooling gives a fresh finish. A strawberry ice is a strawberry flavor with a chill, not a mint. Some ice flavors use little menthol taste, and others are noticeably minty. Read descriptions, and try one to see. See [mint vape flavors](/blog/mint-vape-flavors-guide/) and [menthol vape flavors](/blog/menthol-vape-flavors-guide/).

## How cooling changes fruit flavors
Cooling brightens fruit. It lifts the top notes, makes citrus feel sharper, makes berry flavors feel fresher and cuts through sweetness so that a very sweet flavor feels lighter. In some cases, too much cooling mutes the fruit, because the cold sensation dominates. A light cooling can be a pleasant balance, and a heavy cooling can overpower. That is why makers sell several intensities.

## Intensity levels
Names give clues. "Ice" or "chill" usually means a moderate cooling. "Freeze", "arctic", "polar" and "blast" suggest a strong one. "Frost" can mean in between. There is no standard, and each brand uses words differently. If you are sensitive to cold, start with a plain version or a light "ice". If you love a strong chill, try a "freeze" or "arctic". Our catalog lists many ice flavors; see [ice vape flavors](/blog/ice-vape-flavors-guide/).

## Where you feel it
Cooling is often felt on the inhale, in the mouth and throat, and again on the exhale through the nose. Some products feel cold at the front of the mouth, others at the back of the throat. It can linger for a few seconds. Some people notice it more in the first puffs, and less later, as the sense adapts.

## Cooling and throat hit
Cooling can make a hit feel sharper, because cold and irritation are processed together. A cooling flavor with high nicotine can feel harsher than a plain one. If you find an ice flavor harsh, try a plain version at the same strength, or a lighter cooling. See [throat hit explained](/blog/throat-hit-explained/).

## Cooling and coils
Cooling agents are used in small amounts, and they can leave residue on coils, as can sweeteners. Ice flavors may shorten coil life a little in refillable devices, but the effect is modest. Replace coils when flavor fades; see [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/).

## Who prefers plain flavors
People who find cold sensations uncomfortable, who have sensitive teeth or throats, who prefer the full sweetness of a fruit or who find that cooling dulls flavor often choose plain versions. Others like the contrast of fruit and chill. Neither is right or wrong. Try both of the same flavor to learn your preference.

## How to choose
1. Pick a flavor family you enjoy.
2. Try the plain version and an ice version, as single units.
3. Notice whether cooling brightens or masks the fruit.
4. Note how long the cooling lasts and whether it bothers you.
5. Try a stronger or lighter version if needed.

See [best disposable vapes for flavor lovers](/blog/best-disposable-vapes-for-flavor-lovers/) for a method of choosing.

## A worked example
You like watermelon. You try a watermelon without ice, and find it sweet and soft. You try a watermelon ice, and the chill makes it feel crisp and juicy. You then try a "watermelon freeze", and the cooling is stronger than you like. You decide that "ice" is your level. You buy a 5-pack of the watermelon ice, and keep a plain one for variety. Three single units taught you your preference.

## If cooling is too strong
Choose a plain version, or a lighter one. Lower the power on adjustable devices, open the airflow and take gentler puffs. Rinse your mouth with water. If a particular product feels uncomfortable, stop using it, and keep the device away from children and pets until you recycle it.

## Common mistakes
- **Assuming ice means the same across brands.**
- **Buying a pack of a strong ice flavor untried.**
- **Mixing high nicotine and strong cooling if you are sensitive.**
- **Judging a flavor in one puff.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is the vapor actually cold?
No. The sensation comes from compounds that trigger cold receptors.

### Do ice flavors contain menthol?
Often they use menthol or similar cooling compounds, in varying amounts.

### Do ice flavors have more nicotine?
No. Cooling does not change nicotine content.

### Why does the cooling fade?
The sensation adapts, and flavor and coil change over time. Rotate flavors.

### Can I get cooling without mint taste?
Yes. Many ice flavors use cooling with little mint taste.

## Shop
Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Reading product names for cooling clues
Names are the best guide, and they are not perfect. Words such as "ice", "iced" and "chill" tend to signal a moderate cooling. "Freeze", "frozen", "arctic", "glacier" and "polar" tend to signal strong cooling. "Frost" and "cool" often sit in the middle. Terms such as "menthol" or "mint" signal a minty taste with cooling. Descriptions that mention "a cooling finish" or "refreshing exhale" usually mean light cooling. If a product page lists a cooling level, such as light, medium or strong, use it. If it does not, look at the reviews, if any, or buy a single unit before a pack. We do not publish ratings that are not real, so if a product has no review, we will not make one up.

## Pairing cooling with flavor families
Cooling suits some families more than others. Citrus and berry flavors often gain from it, because the chill lifts acidity. Melon and tropical flavors pair well, because the cooling mimics the sensation of cold fruit. Creamy and dessert flavors often lose character with heavy cooling, though a light touch can make a milkshake or a custard feel fresher. Tobacco flavors rarely use cooling, apart from menthol tobacco blends. If you are unsure, start with a berry or melon ice, and move outward.

## Cooling and the exhale
Many people notice the cooling most on the exhale through the nose, where the sensation is strong and brief. Others feel it as a cold ring across the roof of the mouth. If you do not like the nasal sensation, exhale through the mouth, or choose a lighter cooling. The way you inhale also matters: a slow draw spreads the sensation, and a fast draw concentrates it.

## Building a rotation with cooling
If you enjoy both plain and cooling flavors, a simple rotation keeps flavor from fading. For example, use a plain fruit in the morning, an ice version in the afternoon and a dessert flavor in the evening. The contrast resets your palate, and each flavor tastes stronger than it would if you used it all day. See [vape flavor fading fixes](/blog/vape-flavor-fading-fixes/) for more rotation schemes.

## Cooling in other products
Cooling agents also appear in nicotine pouches, where "mint" and "ice" blends are common, and in some liquids for refillable devices. The same principles apply: they change the sensation, not the nicotine content, and different brands use different intensities. If you try a pouch or a liquid with cooling, begin with a lower strength and a lighter cooling.

## Storing cooling flavors
Cooling flavors keep well when stored properly. Keep devices upright, cool and out of direct sun, and keep liquid bottles tightly capped. Menthol and cooling agents can fade a little with heat, so a bottle left in a warm car may taste flatter and less cool than a fresh one. If a cooling flavor seems to have lost its chill, check the storage first, then the coil, then the device battery.

## Trying cooling flavors in small steps
If you have never tried cooling, start with the lightest version in a flavor you know well. Use it for a few days. If you like it, try a stronger one. If you do not, return to plain. Moving in small steps means you never end up with a pack of something you dislike, and you learn your own preference quickly. Keep notes, and share them with us if you would like help choosing the next product.
